title: MRIS
subtitle: Mountain Rescue Information System
summary: Enterprise mountain rescue information system for backend development and production maintenance.

overview.title: Overview
paragraphs: MRIS is the primary production system I work on as a Software Development Engineer at eZoom Information.
I contribute to full-stack feature development, production maintenance, system integration, and deployment while working within a large existing enterprise application.

responsibilities.title: Responsibilities
items: Develop and maintain full-stack features across Vue frontends and .NET backend services within a large production system.
Participate in system analysis, feature planning, database design, and REST API implementation throughout the development lifecycle.
Design and optimize PostgreSQL data models and implement business workflows including CRUD operations, search, filtering, and pagination.
Deploy, maintain, and troubleshoot applications running on Windows Server and IIS, ensuring reliable production operation.
Investigate and resolve issues spanning frontend, backend APIs, databases, authentication, routing, and deployment environments.
Continuously improve system maintainability through incremental enhancements, technical documentation, and architectural refinements.

technical_highlights.title: Technical Highlights
paragraphs: The system uses a Vue client backed by .NET REST services and PostgreSQL persistence, with application routing and integration boundaries connecting multiple services.
highlights: Vue interfaces communicate with domain APIs through defined REST contracts.
.NET services coordinate business workflows and PostgreSQL data access.
Authentication and permission checks protect role-specific operations.
Reverse-proxy and application routing connect independently deployed services.

items.title: Evolving a large existing system
items.description: Changes must fit established contracts and user workflows, so implementation favors small, reviewable improvements over disruptive rewrites.

items.title: Cross-service integration
items.description: Features can cross frontend, API, data, and routing boundaries, requiring careful interface coordination and end-to-end verification.

items.title: Production diagnosis
items.description: Failures may originate in application logic, database access, reverse-proxy routing, or environment configuration, so troubleshooting follows the complete request path.

outcome.title: Outcome
paragraphs: The application is maintained in a production Windows Server and IIS environment, with reverse-proxy and application-routing configuration supporting its services.
highlights: Coordinate controlled releases for frontend and backend changes.
Verify application routing, API availability, and database connectivity after deployment.
Use production observations to isolate faults and guide maintainability improvements.

lessons_learned.title: Lessons Learned
items: Reliability work requires understanding the entire request path, not only application code.
Stable contracts and incremental delivery reduce risk in a mature enterprise system.
Clear documentation and repeatable diagnosis make cross-service maintenance more effective.
